story.title: Hostage Situation in Cartagena, Colombia Following Failed Robbery
story.summary: Armed men have taken at least 25 hostages in a supermarket in Cartagena, Colombia, after a failed attempt to rob an armored truck. Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella described the assailants as 'common criminals' and confirmed that police and military forces have been deployed to manage the situation as it unfolds.

explore_lenses.title: The incident was still an active standoff
explore_lenses.summary: Authorities confirmed an armed takeover at the Éxito La Castellana supermarket after an attempted armored-truck robbery, but key details remained fluid as of November 24, 2026.

claims.text: President Abelardo de la Espriella said the armed men entered the supermarket after a failed attempt to rob an armored truck and described them as common criminals.
Reports said at least five elderly women had been released, while officials' public estimates of those initially held ranged from about 25 to 30.
The number and identities of people still inside, the assailants' identities, and whether any demands would be verified by authorities were unresolved.

explore_lenses.label: Who is affected beyond the people inside?
explore_lenses.title: The emergency also disrupted airport operations
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate risk is to the hostages, store workers, customers and responding personnel, while the location of the standoff also briefly affected Cartagena air travel.

claims.text: Local reporting described those believed to be held as supermarket customers and employees, although officials had not released a full list or confirmed identities.

Rafael Núñez International Airport temporarily restricted landings because the police operation was near the runway-01 approach path; Colombia's civil-aviation authority later said takeoffs and landings had resumed normally.
Grupo Éxito said protecting people's lives and integrity was its priority and that official updates should come through the competent authorities.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next in the police response?
explore_lenses.title: Authorities say the priority is a safe resolution
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate process is a specialized police-and-security operation focused on protecting people inside and securing the surrounding area, rather than a publicly announced timeline for an assault or negotiation.

claims.text: The president said special units and the capabilities of Colombia's security forces had been deployed to the scene.

Cartagena police said they had activated specialized capabilities and were seeking a safe solution that protects everyone involved; this is the stated operational objective, not a guarantee of outcome or timing.
Cartagena Mayor Dumek Turbay said protocols for this type of event had been implemented and urged the public to be patient, prudent and respectful.
No authority cited in the reporting provided a confirmed timetable for release of the remaining hostages, arrests, or the end of the standoff.

story_report.summary: Armed men took at least 25 people hostage inside a supermarket in Cartagena after a failed attempt to rob an armored truck, according to reports and Colombian authorities. President Abelardo de la Espriella described the assailants as common criminals and said police, military personnel and specialized security capabilities had been deployed. The standoff also temporarily affected air traffic at Cartagena’s Rafael Núñez International Airport, where authorities restricted landings before later resuming normal operations.

sections.heading: Hostage Numbers and Released Captives
sections.body: Preliminary accounts varied on how many people were initially being held, with public estimates ranging from about 25 to 30. Reports said at least five elderly women had been released. Local reporting described those believed to be inside as supermarket customers and employees, but officials had not published a complete list or confirmed their identities.

sections.heading: Security Response and Airport Operations
sections.body: Cartagena police said specialized capabilities had been activated as officers sought a safe solution protecting everyone involved, while Mayor Dumek Turbay said protocols for such incidents were in place and called for patience and prudence. The airport restricted landings because the police operation was near the runway-01 approach path. Colombia’s civil-aviation authority later said takeoffs and landings had resumed normally, though some passengers could still face schedule changes or related disruptions.

unresolved.text: Authorities had not publicly identified the assailants or verified any demands, and the number and identities of people still inside remained unclear.
No confirmed timetable was provided for releases, arrests or the end of the standoff; the method of any resolution and potential criminal charges also remained unconfirmed.

related_stories.title: Nicolas Sarkozy and Carla Bruni to Stand Trial for Witness Tampering
related_stories.summary: Former French President Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife, Carla Bruni, are scheduled to face trial in 2027. They are facing allegations of criminal conspiracy and witness tampering related to illegal campaign funding from Libya during Sarkozy's 2007 election campaign. This follows Sarkozy's imprisonment last year for separate charges.

related_stories.title: Trump Awards Presidential Medal of Freedom to Rudy Giuliani
related_stories.summary: President Donald Trump has awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom to Rudy Giuliani, the former mayor of New York City, recognizing his leadership during the 9/11 attacks. Giuliani, who has been a close ally of Trump and served as his personal lawyer, has faced controversy for his role in efforts to overturn the 2020 presidential election results. The award ceremony took place in the Oval Office.
